newsitem.title: USA: Nutrition for Life awarded injunction.
newsitem.headline: Nutrition for Life awarded injunction.

text.p: Nutrition For Life International Inc said Tuesday that an injunction has been rendered in favor of the company, its Chief Executive David Betrand and Executive Vice President Jana Mitcham in their libel suit against Greg Caton.
The company said a judge in Harris County Court, Texas, awarded $124 million to the company and $4.6 million each to Bertrand and Mitcham.

Caton subsequently declared bankruptcy, the company said. The presiding bankruptcy judge has permitted the Permanent Injunction, but has not yet permitted the entry of the money judgments, the company said.
Caton is a former shareholder of Consumer Express Inc, a predecessor of Nutrition for Life. He could not be reached for comment.
The company said the judgment orders that Caton and his associates are restrained from making any communication about Nutrition For Life International or any director or officer of the company.

The company said the final judgment also orders that Caton immediately remove all editions of his book "MLM Fraud: A Practical Handbook for the Network Marketing Professional" from distribution and that he will not republish or redistribute the book.
